title: Governance and organisation
summary: The management body defines, approves, oversees and is accountable for the ICT risk management framework. It sets roles, budget, the digital operational resilience strategy and the policy on ICT third-party arrangements, and keeps its ICT risk knowledge current.
typical_evidence: Management body approvals; ICT risk roles; training records; budget

title: ICT risk management framework
summary: A sound, documented ICT risk management framework (strategies, policies, procedures, protocols and tools) is reviewed at least yearly and after major incidents, has an independent control function and is regularly internally audited, and includes a digital operational resilience strategy.
typical_evidence: ICT risk management framework; annual review; internal audit reports; resilience strategy

title: ICT systems, protocols and tools
summary: ICT systems are appropriate, reliable, sufficient in capacity and technologically resilient.
typical_evidence: Architecture documentation; capacity monitoring; resilience design

title: Identification
summary: Identify, classify and document ICT-supported business functions, information assets, ICT assets, dependencies and third-party links; assess risks at least yearly and on major change.
typical_evidence: Asset and function inventory; dependency mapping; annual ICT risk assessment

title: Protection and prevention
summary: Continuously monitor and control security and functioning of ICT systems; ICT security policies, procedures and tools; strong authentication; access control; patch and change management; network and encryption controls.
typical_evidence: ICT security policy; access and MFA exports; change and patch records; encryption

title: Detection
summary: Mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities, including network performance issues and ICT-related incidents, with multiple layers of control and alert thresholds.
typical_evidence: Monitoring and alerting configuration; SIEM

title: Response and recovery
summary: An ICT business continuity policy with response and recovery plans; BIA; continuity plans tested at least yearly; crisis management function and communication plans.
typical_evidence: ICT BCP; BIA; annual tests; crisis communication plan

title: Backup policies, restoration and recovery
summary: Backup policies and restoration procedures; backup systems segregated from source; recovery time and point objectives; redundant ICT capacity; secondary processing site for central counterparties and similar.
typical_evidence: Backup policy; restore tests; RTO and RPO; segregation

title: Learning and evolving
summary: Post-incident reviews after major incidents; lessons from tests and real incidents; ICT security awareness and digital operational resilience training for all staff and the management body.
typical_evidence: Post-incident reviews; lessons learned; training records

title: Communication
summary: Crisis communication plans for responsible disclosure of major incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparts and the public; a designated communication role.
typical_evidence: Crisis communication plan; spokesperson role

title: Simplified ICT risk management framework
summary: Small and non-interconnected entities and certain exempt entities apply a simplified ICT risk management framework instead of Articles 5 to 15.
typical_evidence: Only if the entity qualifies for the simplified regime

title: ICT-related incident management process
summary: Define, establish and implement a process to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents; record all incidents and significant cyber threats; early warning indicators; roles; communication.
typical_evidence: Incident management procedure; incident register
category: Ch III Incident management and reporting

title: Classification of ICT-related incidents and cyber threats
summary: Classify incidents and threats on criteria such as clients affected, duration, geographic spread, data losses, criticality of services and economic impact.
typical_evidence: Classification criteria aligned with the RTS; classified incident records
category: Ch III Incident management and reporting

title: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents
summary: Report major incidents to the competent authority: an initial notification, an intermediate report and a final report within the timelines set in the RTS (initial within 4 hours of classification and 24 hours of awareness; intermediate within 72 hours; final within one month); inform affected clients.
typical_evidence: Reporting procedure with RTS timelines; templates; submission records
category: Ch III Incident management and reporting

title: Operational or security payment-related incidents
summary: Credit, payment and e-money institutions apply the incident reporting requirements to payment-related incidents.
typical_evidence: Only for credit, payment, account information or e-money institutions
category: Ch III Incident management and reporting

title: Digital operational resilience testing programme
summary: A sound, comprehensive, risk-based testing programme for ICT systems, run by independent parties; critical ICT systems tested at least yearly.
typical_evidence: Testing programme; annual test results for critical systems

title: Testing of ICT tools and systems
summary: Testing includes vulnerability assessments and scans, open source analyses, network security assessments, gap analyses, physical security reviews, source code reviews, scenario-based tests, compatibility, performance, end-to-end and penetration testing.
typical_evidence: Vulnerability scans; pen tests; code reviews; scenario tests

title: Threat-led penetration testing (TLPT)
summary: Entities identified by competent authorities carry out TLPT at least every three years on critical functions in live production, including relevant ICT third parties.
typical_evidence: Only for entities designated for TLPT

title: Requirements for TLPT testers
summary: TLPT testers are suitable, reputable, certified and insured; external testers are used at least every three tests.
typical_evidence: Only for TLPT: tester qualifications and contracts

title: ICT third-party risk as part of ICT risk management
summary: Manage ICT third-party risk as an integral part of ICT risk management under a strategy and policy on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions, reviewed regularly by the management body.
typical_evidence: ICT third-party risk strategy and policy

title: Register of information
summary: Maintain and update a register of information on all contractual arrangements for ICT services from ICT third-party providers, distinguishing critical or important functions; report it to the competent authority on request and yearly on new arrangements.
typical_evidence: Register of information in the ITS template

title: Pre-contract assessment and due diligence
summary: Before contracting, assess whether the service supports a critical or important function, the supervisory conditions, the provider's suitability, conflicts of interest and concentration risk.
typical_evidence: Pre-contract assessments; due diligence records

title: Termination rights
summary: Contracts can be terminated in cases such as significant breach, circumstances that alter performance, weaknesses in ICT risk management, or supervisory inability.
typical_evidence: Contract termination clauses

title: Exit strategies
summary: Exit strategies for ICT services supporting critical or important functions, with comprehensive, documented and tested exit plans.
typical_evidence: Exit plans; exit tests

title: Preliminary assessment of ICT concentration risk
summary: When contracting for critical or important functions, assess concentration risk, including substitutability, multiple contracts with the same provider and subcontracting chains.
typical_evidence: Concentration risk assessment

title: Key contractual provisions for all ICT services
summary: Contracts include the service description, data locations, data protection, access and return of data on termination, service levels, assistance with incidents, cooperation with authorities, termination rights and participation in awareness programmes.
typical_evidence: Contract clause review against Art 30(2); for ICT suppliers: customer DORA addendum

title: Additional provisions for critical or important functions
summary: For critical or important functions, contracts also include full service level descriptions, notice and reporting duties, business contingency plans and testing, participation in the customer's TLPT, unrestricted audit and access rights, and exit strategies.
typical_evidence: Contract clause review against Art 30(3); BCP test evidence shared with customers

title: Information-sharing arrangements
summary: Entities may share cyber threat information and intelligence within trusted communities, notifying the competent authority of participation.
typical_evidence: Only if participating in information-sharing arrangements
